activity.instructions.source: The Hillford council has ideas for using AI. Put each idea in the group you would recommend. There is no score, and more than one answer can make sense. After you place one, you see one possible answer and a reason. Then, as a separate point, you see what the European Union (EU) AI law says.
activity.instructions.back: The Hillford town council has some ideas for using AI. Put each idea in the group you propose. There is no score, and more than one answer can make sense. After you place one idea, you see one possible answer and its reason. Then, as a separate point, you see what the European Union (EU) AI law says.
activity.instructions.note: "EU" is "UE" (Uni Eropa), the Indonesian abbreviation, spelled out once here and in the reading.

activity.items.0.text.source: A tool gives every person a “good citizen” score. The score decides who gets help.
activity.items.0.text.back: A tool gives every person a “good citizen” score. The score decides who gets help.

activity.items.0.feedback.back: A score like this can be unfair to whole groups. In the EU, the law bans scores like this.

activity.items.1.text.source: A camera in class reads students' faces to guess how they feel.
activity.items.1.text.back: A camera in class reads students' faces to guess their feelings.

activity.items.1.feedback.source: Feelings are private, and guesses can be wrong. Some say it could spot a student who needs help. In the EU, the law bans this in schools, except for health or safety.
activity.items.1.feedback.back: Feelings are private, and guesses can be wrong. Some say the camera could find a student who needs help. In the EU, the law bans this in schools, except for health or safety reasons.

activity.items.4.feedback.source: A mistake could harm someone's health, so a nurse or doctor should check. In the EU, the law counts many health tools as high risk.
activity.items.4.feedback.back: A mistake could harm someone's health, so a nurse or doctor should check. In the EU, the law considers many health tools high-risk.

activity.items.5.text.back: A tool sorts reports about broken street lights. The tool sends each report to the right team.

activity.items.5.feedback.source: It can help reports reach the right team faster, and people still fix the lights. A real tool like this works in Thailand. Strict rules could make sense too, if it decides whose problem comes first.
activity.items.5.feedback.back: This tool can help reports reach the right team faster, and humans still repair the lights. A real tool like this is used in Thailand. Strict rules could also make sense, if the tool decides whose problem comes first.

read.sections.0.heading.source: Many groups make rules for AI
read.sections.0.heading.back: Many groups make rules for AI

read.sections.0.text.source: New technology brings questions about who it helps, who it might harm and who decides. In the made-up town of Hillford, the council wants to use AI, so it holds a meeting first. A shop owner, students, a nurse, an older neighbour and a newer resident who can't vote all give their views. In the real world, many groups make rules for AI. Governments make laws, which everyone must follow. Companies write rules for their own tools. Groups of countries agree on a guideline, which is advice that countries can choose to use. Residents, including young people, can share their ideas too.
read.sections.0.text.back: New technology brings questions about who it helps, who it might harm, and who decides. In the made-up town of Hillford, the town council wants to use AI, so the council holds a meeting first. A shop owner, students, a nurse, an elderly neighbour and a new resident who can't vote yet all give their opinions. In the real world, many groups make rules for AI. Governments make laws, which everyone must follow. Companies write rules for their own tools. Groups of countries agree on a guideline, which is advice that countries may choose to use. Residents, including young people, can also share their ideas.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: Who does a new tool help or harm? Who decides? In made-up Hillford, the council holds a meeting about AI. Many residents share their views, even some who can't vote. Governments make laws. Everyone must follow a law. Companies make rules for their tools. Groups of countries agree on a guideline. A guideline is advice. Young people can share ideas too.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: Who is helped or harmed by a new tool? Who decides? In the made-up town of Hillford, the town council holds a meeting about AI. Many residents give their opinions, even some who can't vote yet. Governments make laws. Everyone must follow laws. Companies make rules for their tools. Groups of countries agree on guidelines. A guideline is advice. Young people can also share ideas.

read.sections.1.heading.source: Guidelines, a law and levels of risk
read.sections.1.heading.back: Guidelines, laws and levels of risk

read.sections.1.text.source: In 2021, all 193 member states of UNESCO adopted the first global agreement on the ethics of AI, which says AI should protect human rights and stay under human control. In 2024, the countries of ASEAN in Southeast Asia shared a guide for AI, with ideas such as fairness, privacy and safety. Both are guidelines. The European Union (EU) made a law that came into force in August 2024, with parts starting on different dates. It sorts uses of AI by risk, which means how much harm they could do. Some uses are banned, such as scores that treat people unfairly. Some are high risk, such as marking exams, so they need strict checks. Most uses, like spam filters, have no special AI rules, but other laws, like privacy laws, still apply.
read.sections.1.text.back: In 2021, UNESCO's 193 member states approved the first global agreement on the ethics of AI, which says AI must protect human rights and stay under human control. In 2024, the ASEAN countries in Southeast Asia shared a guide for AI, with ideas such as fairness, privacy and safety. Both are guidelines. The European Union (EU) made a law that came into force in August 2024, with parts that come into force on different dates. That law groups uses of AI by their risk, meaning how much harm they could cause. Some uses are banned, such as scores that treat people unfairly. Some are high-risk, such as marking exams, so they need strict checks. Most uses, such as junk message filters, have no special AI rules, but other laws, such as laws about privacy, still apply.

Risk means how much harm it could do. Some uses are banned, like unfair scores. Some are high risk, like marking exams. Most uses have no special AI rules. But other laws, like privacy laws, still apply.

read.sections.2.heading.source: A real service, and your own view
read.sections.2.heading.back: A real service, and your own opinion

read.sections.2.text.source: In Thailand, people report problems such as broken roads, floods or street lights on Traffy Fondue, a public platform built by a national science agency. Its AI sorts each report and sends it to the right office, where people still decide what to do and fix it. Its makers say it received over 940,000 reports in two years. That shows many people use it, not how well each problem was solved. What a law says is one answer. Your own recommendation can be different, if you give reasons.
read.sections.2.text.back: In Thailand, people report problems such as broken roads, floods or street lights on Traffy Fondue, a public platform made by a national science agency. Its AI sorts each report and sends it to the right office, where humans still decide what to do and repair it. Its makers say the platform received more than 940,000 reports in two years. That number shows that many people use it, not how well each problem was solved. What a law says is one answer. Your own proposal can be different, as long as you give reasons.

watch.summary.source: This video is from UNESCO. UNESCO is a world group that works on schools, science and culture. The video is part of a series about the ethics of AI. Ethics means what is right and wrong. The video asks a big question. How can people get the good things from AI without making gaps between people bigger? AI could also bring new kinds of unfair results. The video says people around the world seem to agree on some ideas. These include privacy, equal treatment and leaving no one out. The hard part is turning these ideas into real rules. The video looks at how different parts of the world are making rules for AI. It also asks what would make rules fair for everyone, everywhere.

The hard part is turning these ideas into real rules. The video looks at how different parts of the world make rules for AI. It also asks what would make those rules fair for everyone, everywhere.

sensitiveNotes.0.source: Rules about cameras, scores and surveillance can be close to home for learners who have lived under heavy policing, in camps or at borders. Keep the discussion on made-up Hillford. Never ask learners about the laws, police or government of any country they have lived in, or how they were checked or recorded; let them speak only if they choose to.
sensitiveNotes.0.back: Rules about cameras, scores and surveillance can feel close for learners who have lived under strict police surveillance, in camps or at borders. Keep the discussion on made-up Hillford. Never ask learners about the laws, police or government of any country they have lived in, or how they were checked or recorded; let them speak only if they themselves want to.

educatorNotes.0.source: Keep two questions apart: “What do you recommend for Hillford?” (the learner's view, marked on reasons) and “What does the European Union's law say?” (a fact about one jurisdiction). Never mark a recommendation wrong because it differs from the EU law. The AI Act (in force 1 August 2024) bans, from 2 February 2025, social scoring that leads to unjustified or unrelated harmful treatment, emotion recognition in workplaces and schools except for medical or safety reasons, and live face identification by police in public places except for three narrow purposes (searching for victims or missing persons, preventing an imminent threat, and finding suspects of serious crimes). Transparency rules (chatbots, labelled deepfakes) apply from August 2026. After the AI Omnibus (in force 27 July 2026), high-risk rules for uses such as exam scoring apply from 2 December 2027, and for AI in regulated products from 2 August 2028; check the Commission's page before quoting dates. Minimal-risk uses (spam filters, games) have no AI Act rules, but data protection, consumer protection and product safety law still apply (Article 2). The market-camera item is about police; a council's or shop's face cameras would fall under other rules. Paper version: the nine ideas on cards under three headings.
educatorNotes.0.back: Separate two questions: “What do you propose for Hillford?” (the learner's opinion, judged on its reasons) and “What does the European Union's law say?” (a fact about one jurisdiction). Never mark a proposal wrong because it differs from the EU law. The AI Act (in force since 1 August 2024) bans, from 2 February 2025, social scoring that leads to harmful treatment that is unjustified or unrelated, emotion recognition in workplaces and schools except for medical or safety reasons, and live face identification by police in public places except for three narrow purposes (looking for victims or missing persons, preventing an imminent threat, and finding suspects of serious crimes). Transparency rules (chatbots, labelled deepfakes) apply from August 2026. After the AI Omnibus (in force since 27 July 2026), high-risk rules for uses such as exam marking apply from 2 December 2027, and for AI in regulated products from 2 August 2028; check the European Commission's page before quoting dates. Minimal-risk uses (junk message filters, games) have no rules in the AI Act, but data protection, consumer protection and product safety law still apply (Article 2). The market camera idea is about police; face cameras belonging to a town council or a shop would be covered by other rules. Paper version: the nine ideas on cards, under three headings.
educatorNotes.0.note: "Data protection" is "pelindungan data" with "pelindungan", the spelling of Indonesia's own law (UU Pelindungan Data Pribadi).

educatorNotes.1.source: Traffy Fondue (Thailand) was developed by NECTEC, part of the National Science and Technology Development Agency (NSTDA). Residents report through a LINE chatbot with a location and photo; since 2024 its AI also summarises reports, ranks them by urgency, suggests fixes and filters rude words, as well as classifying them and sending each to the responsible agency. NSTDA reports more than 940,000 reports from June 2022 to July 2024, over 733,000 of them “completed” (77%), across 77 provinces and more than 15,000 agencies. These are the operator's own figures: completed is a status in the system, not an independent check of repairs. It is an operating service, not a measured impact.
educatorNotes.1.back: Traffy Fondue (Thailand) was developed by NECTEC, part of Thailand's National Science and Technology Development Agency (NSTDA). Residents report through a LINE chatbot with a location and a photo; since 2024 its AI also summarises reports, orders them by urgency, suggests repairs and filters rude words, besides grouping reports and sending each to the responsible agency. NSTDA reports more than 940,000 reports from June 2022 to July 2024, more than 733,000 of them with the status “completed” (77%), in 77 provinces and more than 15,000 agencies. These are the operator's own figures: “completed” is a status in the system, not an independent check of the repairs. It is a running service, not a measured impact.

educatorNotes.2.source: To localise: Indonesia's Minister of Communication and Informatics issued a circular on AI ethics (Surat Edaran No. 9 of 2023), and Malaysia launched voluntary national guidelines in 2024 (link in the claim record, content/courses/digital-world/claims/DW16.md). Like the UNESCO and ASEAN texts, both are guidance rather than laws. Present every approach neutrally; the lesson compares, it doesn't rank countries.
educatorNotes.2.back: For local context: Indonesia's Minister of Communication and Informatics issued a circular letter on AI ethics (Circular Letter No. 9 of 2023), and Malaysia launched voluntary national guidelines in 2024 (the link is in the claim record, content/courses/digital-world/claims/DW16.md). Like the UNESCO and ASEAN texts, both are guidance, not laws. Present every approach neutrally; this lesson compares, it does not rank countries.
